newsitem.title: USA: White House lists guests on presidential plane.
newsitem.headline: White House lists guests on presidential plane.

text.p: Fifty-six major Democratic Party contributors flew on Air Force One as guests of President Clinton in 1995 and 1996, the White House disclosed Monday.
The White House, in an attempt to defuse questions about campaign fundraising practices, also released the names of 17 contributors who were guests of Vice President Al Gore during the same period.
The contributors either gave at least $5,000 to Clinton's re-election campaign or contributed or raised at least $25,000 for the Democratic National Committee.
Many of those identified are politically active Democrats, including Colorado Gov. Roy Romer, now the party's chairman, and Terry McAuliffe, who served as finance chairman for Clinton's campaign.
According to the White House, 477 persons flew as guests of the president during 1995 and 1996, while Gore served as host for 208 individuals during the same period.

Although the White House only released the names of the individuals without detailed identification, many of them clearly were Democratic Party activists or union leaders, including John Sweeney, president of the AFL-CIO.
Justin Dart, once a key political ally of former President Ronald Reagan and a member of his so-called "kitchen cabinet" of private advisers, also was listed as a donor.
